html:
The Royal Niger Company was a British trading company that ruled the lower Niger from 1886 to 1900. Its lands became the core of colonial Nigeria.

George Goldie merged rival British firms trading for palm oil on the Niger into one company in 1879. He bought out French competitors, and his treaties with local rulers helped Britain claim the region at the Berlin Conference. In 1886 the company got a royal charter to govern, much as the East India Company had done in India.

The company used its power to shut out rivals, including African traders. In 1895 the people of Brass, cut off from their markets, attacked its depot at Akassa. In 1897 its private army conquered the emirates of Nupe and Ilorin on the edge of the Sokoto Caliphate.

Its rule was costly and widely criticised, and on 1 January 1900 the British government took over its territory, which became the protectorates of Northern and Southern Nigeria. The company carried on as a trading firm and later became part of the Unilever group.
sum: The Royal Niger Company was a British trading company that ruled the lower Niger from 1886 to 1900. Its lands became the core of colonial Nigeria.
